core_meaning.short_meaning: Adorned sash of dignity; early heroine and martyr of faith Zunairah al-Rumiyyah.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Zunairah (زُنَيْرَة) is an Arabic feminine given name meaning 'delicate sash of honor', 'adorned belt of dignity', or 'flower of steadfast faith'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Zunairah al-Rumiyyah, an early convert to Islam who endured brutal torture in Mecca until she lost her sight, yet remained unshakeable in faith until Allah miraculously restored her vision.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive of zinnār (a belt or sash of modest beauty), signifying strength, neat elegance, and steadfast commitment.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Zunairah was among the enslaved early converts in Mecca who had no tribal protector. Abu Jahl and other chieftains severely tortured her to force her to renounce Islam, causing her to lose her sight. When the polytheists mocked her claiming their idols took her sight, she proclaimed with supreme courage that idols neither see nor harm and that only Allah has power. The very next morning, Allah restored her eyesight completely. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq then purchased and freed her.
